analysis: The 32-negative sampled-softmax trial achieved validation macro HR@10 of 0.5575, below the prior target-excluded LightGCN result of 0.5613 by 0.0038. Electronics improved slightly from 0.360 to 0.365 but remained below the cited 0.420 baseline. Category HR@10 was 0.575 for Movies_and_TV, 0.595 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.365 for Electronics, and 0.695 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Execution succeeded, but this trial does not support replacing BPR with this sampled-softmax configuration. Stronger negative competition did not improve the aggregate result; the metrics do not establish why. No held-out test results were used.
code_summary: Four separate 64-dimensional, two-layer LightGCN models use normalized user-item graphs and average embeddings across the initial and propagated layers. Training adds a coefficient-0.5 history profile with a 10-interaction half-life, differentiably excluding every occurrence of the positive item and zeroing profiles with no remaining items. The objective is temperature-1 cross-entropy over one positive and 32 uniformly sampled unseen negatives with replacement. Raw embedding regularization remains 1e-4, averaging negative squared norms across draws. Adam uses learning rate 0.003, batch size 8192, eight steps per epoch, and gradient clipping at 5.0. Exported graph embeddings and history-aware inference remain unchanged, including all four dataset routes and the predictor writer.
